narrative.headline: OFAC sanctions Sudan network after silence, targeting port and tech firms
narrative.body: OFAC designated TARGET MULTIACTIVITIES COMPANY LTD, PORTS ENGINEERING COMPANY LTD, and linked individual Tariq Hussain Muhammad Madani on July 1, 2026, after a recorded gap in Sudan filings. The cluster connects a ports engineering firm to Sudan Master Technology, suggesting a sanctions-evasion network using infrastructure and tech companies.
narrative.prompt: I just saw that OFAC sanctioned three entities linked to Sudan on July 1, 2026 — TARGET MULTIACTIVITIES COMPANY LTD, PORTS ENGINEERING COMPANY LTD (linked to SUDAN MASTER TECHNOLOGY), and an individual named Tariq Hussain Muhammad Madani — after a period of silence on Sudan filings. Why does this matter? Sudan is under broad U.S. sanctions, and new designations after a gap often signal fresh intelligence on evasion networks. Who benefits from these companies, and what does the ports-technology connection suggest about how sanctioned goods or funds move? Is SUDAN MASTER TECHNOLOGY a previously designated entity? What should I watch for next — specifically, are there related front companies, shipping routes, or financial intermediaries that could face follow-on designations?

narrative.headline: OFAC ties Russian firm AVRATEK to Iranian IRGC procurement network
narrative.body: OFAC simultaneously sanctioned Russian entity AVRATEK OOO, its associate Druzhbin, and Russian national Selina linked to Iran's IRGC — all on the same date. The mechanism is a Russia-Iran sanctions evasion network using AVRATEK as a procurement front for IRGC-linked operative Behrouz Namazi.
narrative.prompt: I just saw that OFAC sanctioned a Russian company called AVRATEK OOO alongside two Russian individuals — Vadim Druzhbin (linked to AVRATEK) and Mariya Selina (linked to Iran's IRGC) — all on the same date. This matters because it suggests a Russia-based front company is helping Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps evade sanctions, potentially for weapons or dual-use technology procurement. Who is Behrouz Namazi and what is his role in IRGC procurement? How does AVRATEK fit into known Russia-Iran sanctions evasion networks? Is this pattern of Russian nationals facilitating IRGC procurement growing or isolated? Watch for follow-on designations of AVRATEK's suppliers, customers, or financial intermediaries — that would confirm an active, expanding network rather than a one-off bust.
